card.name: Noun or verb before an expected 'and' clause
card.fires_on: Ordinary words in general prose, often a noun or verb right before a continuation such as 'and', 'or' or a following clause. Examples are history, cause, assemble, subject, cells and parent, often in genetics or civic text.

modes.description: Nouns such as cells, parent or parents in explanations of inheritance and genetic conditions.

modes.description: A comma after 'have been reported' before a 'both ... and' phrase.
